title: Building and Using a U.S. Polar Defense Industrial Base
gist: CSIS argues decades of neglect have left the US polar defense industrial base (icebreakers, LC-130 Skibirds, C-17s) too old and thin to counter rising China-Russia Arctic and Antarctic activity; recent contracts for 11 Arctic Security Cutters ($3.5B + $3.3B), $4.3B for Polar Security Cutters and LC-130J funding are progress, but Antarctic icebreakers and strategic airlift remain gaps.

insights.claim: China and Russia are deepening polar cooperation, conducting joint military and scientific missions in the Arctic, pioneering a commercial shipping route, and coordinating to expand their presence in Antarctica.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Polar competition is a durable driver of US defense and shipbuilding appropriations.

insights.claim: Sustained neglect of the US polar defense industrial base has given competitors the false impression that the US has forgotten the polar regions; aging and shrinking equipment cannot meet stated US goals.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Supports multi-year procurement budgets for polar-capable ships and aircraft.

insights.claim: The US regularly operates only two Arctic icebreakers, the USCGC Healy (which recently suffered a major mechanical failure) and the USCGC Storis (a converted commercial vessel bought in 2024), and a single 50-year-old heavy icebreaker, the Polar Star, for Antarctica.

insights.so_what: Acute capability gap underpins urgency of icebreaker procurement.

insights.claim: Boeing ended C-17 Globemaster III production in 2015, costing over 5,000 jobs, and no successor strategic airlifter exists; restarting the line would cost an estimated $8 billion, though Boeing is reportedly pursuing a restart and the FY2027 NDAA would require an Air Force report on a next-generation airlifter.

insights.claim: The LC-130 Skibird's unique ability to land on snow and ice lets the US operate the second-largest Antarctic station at the geographic South Pole and gives flexibility in infrastructure-poor Arctic areas including Greenland.

insights.so_what: Ski-equipped airlift is strategically irreplaceable, supporting durable funding.

insights.claim: The US should build a polar defense industrial base producing both heavy and medium icebreakers and research vessels domestically, procure enough LC-130J aircraft and expedite a next-generation C-17, as the nucleus of a unified polar strategy that also creates thousands of US jobs.

insights.claim: The Trump administration has broken decades of stagnation in Arctic icebreaker building but it remains unclear whether it has expanded domestic capacity for Antarctic heavy icebreakers.
